::: {.callout-note title="Retrospective case study" icon=false}
Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains
no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from
the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.
:::

## Observation

- QQQ fell 3.47% and SPY 1.77%.
- AMD fell 10.88%, SMH 6.98% and NVDA 4.22%. The space group averaged -6.8%.
- Defensives (+1.3%) and healthcare (+0.5%) rose. TLT gained 0.43% and the 10-year yield ended at 4.93%.
- GLD fell 3.47%. The VIX rose 12.9% to 19.4.

## Mechanism

**Channel: cash flows.**

- Intel fell 28.6% after its results, and Amazon's report added to concern about the cost of AI infrastructure.
- Investors questioned whether the industry's capital spending would earn an adequate return.
- That doubt was applied to the whole hardware supply chain, so semiconductors were repriced together.
- Money rotated into defensives and bonds, which is an orderly move away from one theme, not a rush for cash.

The dispersion inside the sector is informative: NVDA fell less than half as much as AMD, so investors were still ranking companies and not selling the group indiscriminately.

**Open question.** Gold fell 3.5% on a day when bonds rose. A safe asset falling alongside equities can indicate selling to cover losses elsewhere. I would need positioning data to confirm it.

## What happened next

Over the following five trading days QQQ fell a further 5.0%, NVDA 8.8% and AMD 11.0%. The selling continued.

## Lesson

Compare this with July 29. A geopolitical shock reversed within days because the feared event did not happen. A repricing based on doubts about cash flows persisted, because nothing arrived to answer the doubt. The cause of a selloff says a lot about how long it lasts.
